newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus parliament ratifies company merger law.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus parliament ratifies company merger law.

text.p: Parliament in Cyprus on Thursday ratified legislation regulating equal treatment among shareholders in bid situations.
The legislation was approved with a majority in the 56-seat house with only one absention and one vote against.

It regulates the procedures by which mergers or acquisitions should be handled by public companies on the Cyprus bourse, and ensures that minority shareholders are not excluded from bids by enforcing that prospective buyers make offers to all shareholders on a pro-rata basis.
"It completes a vaccum that should never have existed in the first place," socialist Edek party deputy Takis Hadjidemetriou told parliament.
The Cyprus Stock Exchange, which started working under an official framework in March 1996, trades in 91 securities through 41 listings.
Based on European Union directives, the regulations also give third parties the ability to make counter offers within a set time span.

Deputies dismissed a suggestion by centre-right Democratic Party deputy Marcos Kyprianou to put the legislation on hold for another week pending recommendations for its improvement from another party member who was absent.

The legislation, which amends 1993 stock exchange regulations, set penalties of up to two years in prison or a fine of up to 5,000 pounds, ($9,900) or both for those failing to comply. ($=0.506 pounds)
